entities.summary: Diego Hurtado de Mendoza y de la Cerda, 1st Duke of Francavilla, was a Spanish nobleman who played a pivotal role in the politics and society of Renaissance Italy. He was the son of Diego Hurtado de Mendoza, 2nd Duke of Francavilla, and Maria de Salazar, and succeeded his father as duke of Francavilla in 1567. Mendoza y de la Cerda's tenure as duke was marked by his efforts to maintain the independence of the Duchy of Montferrat, which he had inherited from his father. He also played a key role in the Italian Wars, serving as a commander in the Spanish army during the Siege of Pavia in 1525. Mendoza y de la Cerda's legacy extends beyond his military achievements, as he was a patron of the arts and a supporter of the Renaissance humanist movement. He was particularly close to the Italian poet and statesman, Ludovico Ariosto, and the two men collaborated on several literary projects. Mendoza y de la Cerda's impact on Italian history can be seen in the many cities and towns he founded, including the city of Francavilla, which became a major center of commerce and culture in the region. He died in 1578, leaving behind a legacy as one of the most important figures of the Renaissance in Italy.
